response.sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT pc.product_type_description AS d, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty, AVG(ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_diff FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = ili.product_id JOIN Product_Categories pc ON pc.production_type_code = p.production_type_code GROUP BY pc.product_type_description), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) AS mean_diff FROM cat) SELECT AVG(cat.avg_qty) AS avg_of_avg_quantity, AVG(cat.avg_diff) AS avg_of_avg_cost_diff, AVG(cat.avg_diff - m.mean_diff) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM cat CROSS JOIN m WHERE cat.avg_diff > m.mean_diff

assumptions.assumption: Inner joins drop unmatched lines. Categories are grouped by product_type_description, as the request says. If two category codes share a description, they merge into one group.
product_quantity is stored as text, so it is cast to a number before averaging. Rows with a NULL cost difference are ignored in the cost-difference average, because AVG skips NULLs.
The mean is the unweighted average of the category averages. Categories with no non-null cost difference are excluded from it.
